name: LM339DT
title: LM139, LM239, LM339: low-power quad voltage comparators
summary: Four independent voltage comparators in one package, each with a PNP input stage whose common-mode range reaches down to ground and an open-collector output. They run from one supply of 2 V to 32 V, or split supplies of ±1 V to ±16 V, drawing about 1.1 mA for all four whatever the supply voltage. The LM139, LM239 and LM339 differ in operating temperature range; the A grades have a tighter offset, 2 mV maximum. LM339DT is the 0 °C to +70 °C standard grade in SO14 on tape and reel.

notes: (1) The output current limits at about 20 mA whatever VCC+ is. A short from the output to VCC+ (rather than to ground) can overheat and destroy the part.
(2) Typical values. Short circuits can overheat the part.
(3) HBM: 100 pF charged to the rated voltage and discharged through 1.5 kΩ, applied between every pair of connected pins with the remaining pins left open.
(4) MM: 200 pF charged to the rated voltage and discharged straight between two pins, no series resistor (under 5 Ω internal), for every pair of connected pins with the rest open.
(5) CDM: the whole package and all pins charged together, then discharged to ground through a single pin, repeated for each pin.

notes: (1) Measured with the output at its switching point, Vo ≈ 1.4 V, for VCC+ anywhere from 5 V to 30 V and over all common-mode voltages between 0 V and VCC+ -1.5 V.

(2) The input stage is PNP, so the bias current flows out of the input pins. It stays essentially the same whichever state the output is in, so it puts no changing load on the reference or input lines.
(3) Neither input may go more than 0.3 V below ground. The common-mode range tops out at VCC+ -1.5 V, yet one or both inputs can be taken to +30 V without harm.

(4) An input may rise above the supply; the output stays correct provided the other input is inside the common-mode range. The low side of an input must stay at or above -0.3 V, or 0.3 V under the negative supply when one is used.
(5) Measured with 5 mV of overdrive on a 100 mV input step. With larger overdrive the response is 300 ns.

circuits.title: Figure 8. Basic comparator
circuits.description: The simplest use: one comparator on a 5 V supply compares +V(ref) with -V(ref), and a 15 kΩ resistor to the supply pulls the open-collector output VO up.
notes: One comparator of the four is used; VCC+ is on the positive rail and VCC- on ground.

circuits.title: Figure 9. Driving CMOS
circuits.description: The comparator output, pulled to +5 V by 100 kΩ, drives one input of a CMOS NAND gate that shares the same +5 V supply and ground. The gate's other input and its output are the circuit's connections to the rest of the logic.

circuits.title: Figure 11. Low frequency op amp
circuits.description: The comparator used as a low-frequency amplifier with a gain of 100. eI drives the non-inverting input. The output carries a 15 kΩ pull-up to +5 V and 0.5 µF to ground, and 100 kΩ from the output with 1 kΩ to ground return a fraction of it to the inverting input.
notes: One comparator of the four is used; VCC+ is on the positive rail and VCC- on ground.

circuits.title: Figure 12. Low frequency op amp
circuits.description: The same gain-of-100 amplifier with a 2N2222 emitter follower after the filtered output. The 15 kΩ pull-up and 0.5 µF capacitor form the base node, the emitter is the output, and the 100 kΩ / 1 kΩ divider from the emitter closes the loop. eo is 0 V when eI is 0 V.
notes: AV = 100; eo = 0 V for eI = 0 V.
One comparator of the four is used; VCC+ is on the positive rail and VCC- on ground.

circuits.title: Figure 13. Transducer amplifier
circuits.description: A magnetic pick-up coil sits across the two inputs. Two 10 kΩ resistors, one to +5 V and one to ground, bias the non-inverting input and the coil's lower end. A 20 MΩ resistor from the output back to that node gives positive feedback, and 3 kΩ pulls the output up.
notes: One comparator of the four is used; VCC+ is on the positive rail and VCC- on ground.

circuits.title: Figure 14. Time delay generator
circuits.description: All four comparators on +15 V. While the input gating signal is low the first comparator holds the 0.001 µF timing capacitor at ground; when the gate goes high its output lets go and the capacitor charges through 15 kΩ, giving a ramp VC1. The other three comparators watch the ramp against V1, V2 and V3 from a 200 kΩ / 51 kΩ / 51 kΩ / 51 kΩ divider, so VO1, VO2 and VO3 go high in turn at t1, t2 and t3 after the gate's rising edge at t0. Each has 10 kΩ in from the ramp, 10 MΩ of positive feedback and a 3 kΩ pull-up. The first comparator's other input sits on a 10 kΩ / 10 kΩ divider from the supply.
notes: Each output switches from low to VCC+ at its own time: VO1 at t1, VO2 at t2, VO3 at t3, all after the gate rises at t0; the gate falls at tA.
The ramp VC1 crosses V1, V2 and V3 at t1, t2 and t3 and keeps rising to t4.

circuits.title: Figure 15. Low frequency op amp with offset adjust
circuits.description: The amplifier with a 2N2222 output transistor and a 100 kΩ offset trimmer. The trimmer's wiper is on +5 V and its two ends go through 1 MΩ each, one to the non-inverting input and one to the inverting input. The input arrives through R1; RS and R1 together make up R2. A 100 kΩ resistor from the emitter and 1 kΩ to ground feed the inverting input.

parts.note: offset adjust potentiometer: ends 1 and 2, wiper W

notes: RS and R1 carry no values.
One comparator of the four is used; VCC+ is on the positive rail and VCC- on ground.

circuits.title: Figure 16. Zero crossing detector (single power supply)
circuits.description: Detects zero crossings of an input on a single 5 V supply. The input goes through two 5.1 kΩ resistors to the inverting input; a 1N4148 runs from their junction to ground, cathode at the junction. Each input has 100 kΩ to +5 V; the non-inverting one also has 10 kΩ to ground, and 20 MΩ from the output to it gives positive feedback. A 5.1 kΩ resistor pulls the output up.
notes: One comparator of the four is used; VCC+ is on the positive rail and VCC- on ground.

circuits.title: Figure 17. Two-decade high-frequency VCO
circuits.description: Three comparators make a voltage-controlled oscillator with a square wave (output 1) and a triangle wave (output 2). The first comparator has 500 pF from its output to its inverting input, which takes Vcontrol through 100 kΩ; its output, with a 3 kΩ pull-up and 0.01 µF to ground, is the triangle wave. The second takes the triangle through 5.1 kΩ, with 100 kΩ of positive feedback, against VCC+/2 and gives the square wave. The third compares the square wave with VCC+/2 and its output drives the 50 kΩ resistor at the first comparator's inverting input. On 30 V the control range of +250 mV to +50 V sweeps the frequency from 700 Hz to 100 kHz.
notes: Supply VCC+ = +30 V. Control voltage from +250 mV up to +50 V gives fo from 700 Hz up to 100 kHz.

circuits.title: Figure 18. Limit comparator
circuits.description: Two comparators with their outputs tied share one 10 kΩ pull-up on 12 V, which drives the base of a 2N2222; the lamp is between the supply and the collector. eI reaches the inverting input of the upper comparator and the non-inverting input of the lower one through RS; the upper and lower limits come in through 2RS to the other inputs.
notes: Two comparators of the four are used; VCC+ is on the 12 V rail and VCC- on ground.

circuits.title: Figure 19. Crystal-controlled oscillator
circuits.description: A 100 kHz crystal oscillator on 15 V. Two 200 kΩ resistors hold the non-inverting input at half supply and the crystal couples the output back to that node. The inverting input follows the averaged output through 100 kΩ onto 0.1 µF. A 2 kΩ pull-up gives a square wave from 0 to VCC+ at eo.
notes: f = 100 kHz.
One comparator of the four is used; VCC+ is on the positive rail and VCC- on ground.

circuits.title: Figure 20. Zero crossing detector
circuits.description: On ±15 V supplies the inverting input is grounded and eI drives the non-inverting input, so the output, pulled up to +15 V by 5.1 kΩ, changes state each time eI crosses 0 V.
notes: One comparator of the four is used.

circuits.title: Figure 21. Comparator with a negative reference
circuits.description: On ±15 V supplies, eI on the non-inverting input is compared with -5 V on the inverting input; a 5.1 kΩ pull-up to +15 V forms the output.
notes: One comparator of the four is used.

operation.text: Each comparator has a PNP input pair, so its input bias current comes out of the pins and hardly changes when the output switches. The common-mode range starts at ground (0 V) and ends 1.5 V under VCC+ at 25 °C, 2 V under across temperature. Either input can be pulled up to +30 V without damage, and as long as one input stays inside the common-mode range the output is still right. No input should be taken more than 0.3 V below ground, or more than 0.3 V below the negative supply when one is used. The differential input may be as large as the supply voltage.

The output is the open collector of an NPN transistor whose emitter is at VCC-. It sinks 16 mA typical (6 mA minimum) at Vo = 1.5 V, saturates at 250 mV typical with 4 mA, and leaks 0.1 nA typical when off. It is compatible with TTL, DTL, ECL, MOS and CMOS logic.
A short from output to ground can be sustained indefinitely. The output current limits at about 20 mA whatever VCC+ is. A short from output to VCC+ can overheat and destroy the part.
The part runs on a single supply or a split pair. Supply current is about 1.1 mA for all four comparators and changes little with supply voltage: 1.3 mA typical at 30 V.
With a 5.1 kΩ pull-up, the response to a 100 mV step with 5 mV of overdrive takes 1.3 µs typical; larger overdrive brings it to 300 ns, the figure for a TTL-level input against a 1.4 V reference.
